text:
jess: quick follow-up from the operator-laned RFC — thinking about how we split the console query surface into 'lanes' (fast interactive, batch-tiling, and admin-ops). want to capture tradeoffs for RBAC, caching, and SLOs before we write the migration plan.
omar: +1. main concern: RBAC boundaries getting duplicated across lanes. if we push auth into the lane router we risk divergence.
linh: can we keep a single auth layer upstream and pass a capability token to lanes? that way lanes are dumb consumers and we centralize policy. downside: token format/versioning.
ben: token approach sounds clean. also think about cache semantics — fast interactive needs KV prefix cache and low-latency invalidation; tiling wants materialized tiles with longer TTLs. mixing TTLs in a shared cache will be messy.
jess: exact. proposal: central auth -> signed capability header (short lived). lane router handles routing, attaches header. lanes verify signature via public key (no central call). versioned header format like `X-Cap-Token:v1 <sig>` so we can rotate.
omar: what about permission evaluation complexity? e.g., tenant-scoped view vs admin global query. capability needs explicit scope claim. if tile lane receives token without scope it should reject.
linh: agree. tokens should contain scope list + expiry and we should log denied attempts to `console-auth-logs` for audit.
ops-bot: deploy-note: upcoming key rotation window scheduled 2024-08-12 02:00 UTC. expect <1% auth rejects if lanes not updated.
ben: on performance: lane router adds an extra hop. we need tail latency budget: interactive SLO 50ms p95 end-to-end. router must be sub-10ms p95. can we colocate router on same nodes as fast lane executors to avoid network hop?
jess: colocating is feasible for hosted and dedicated. for private on-prem we can't assume. fallback: router has local sticky routing + cross-region fallback. add a health check config to prefer local fast-path.
omar: also think about batching/caching interactions. if router aggregates small requests into a short window for batch lane, that reduces cost but increases latency — need per-route policy.
linh: suggestion: policy DSL attached to routes, e.g., { "lane": "interactive", "max_wait_ms": 8, "batchable": false }. we can version DSL and keep backwards compat.
ben: rollout plan? small canary: create `operator-lanes=v1` flag at route-level, route 5% of traffic for a subset of tenants, metric set: p50/p95 latency, auth rejects, cache hitrate, and cost/tokens per-minute.
jess: agree. add a correctness eval: run stored prompt set against both single-surface and laned routing to detect any divergence in results. if diff > 0.1% we stop. want automation in CI.
omar: migration of existing dashboard queries — some rely on implicit cross-tenant joins that will be blocked by stricter lane tokens. we need compatibility shim: a `cross-join` capability granted only to service accounts. track usage and flag owners.
linh: we should centralize a small compatibility mode in router: if request has `X-Compat:legacy` and tenant in allowlist, router forwards with `legacy` capability. but that weakens security model, so plan to expire after N months.
ben: ops ask: instrumentation — per-request lane label, token version, auth-eval-duration, and route-decisions. expose as traces and metrics. SRE needs a dashboard and alert on auth-reject spike + latency drift.
ess: (typo) meant jess: action items: 1) olin to draft token format + rotation plan (owner: linh). 2) router perf sketch + colocate plan (owner: ben). 3) compatibility allowlist design (owner: omar). 4) CI eval harness for diffs (owner: jess). target: RFC follow-up doc in 2 weeks.
linh: I'll start token schema: fields: `sub`, `scopes[]`, `exp`, `kid`, `sig` and include `issued_by` and `lane_hint` optional claim. will push a sample `proto` in draft.
omar: I'll draft allowlist flow and expiry TTL for legacy mode; propose 90 days max with weekly owner reminders.
ben: I'll prototype a colocated router sidecar and measure p95 for loopback vs network hop. will post numbers.
jess: thanks. one more: backups for key rotation — lanes must fetch JWKs from central store with caching and exponential backoff, but accept stale key for up to 60s to avoid in-flight rejects. document that.
linh: noted. also will add a small CLI snippet to generate tokens for local dev: `console-auth gen-cap --scopes view:tenant:123 --exp 60s --kid testkey`
omar: ok if we also emit an audit event `auth:cap_issued` to `security-audit` with hashed `kid` and scope?
jess: yes, scrub PII and keep hashes. good call.
ops-bot: reminder: schedule runbook update task created (runbook#4521).
ben: final thought: cost tracking — lanes should emit `cost_estimate` per request so billing can map to lane. otherwise dedicated customers will be surprised.
jess: agreed. add `cost_estimate` to metrics contract. wrap-up: I'll assemble follow-up doc with sections: token design, router perf & colocate, lane policies (DSL), cache semantics, compatibility window, rollout checklist, metrics + alerts. ping if you want to own a section.
linh: I'll own token design + dev CLI.
omar: I'll own compatibility and access reviews.
ben: perf + metrics + canary infra.
jess: great — aiming to publish the follow-up RFC by 2024-08-02.
omar: thanks all. :thumbsup:
